sources.entry: DB Browser for SQLite - SQLite database management GUI.

summary.one_liner: DB Browser for SQLite (DB4S) is a visual, open source desktop tool for creating, designing, and editing SQLite-compatible database files.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a spreadsheet-like interface for working with SQLite databases without needing to learn SQL. Listed capabilities include creating and compacting database files, creating, modifying and deleting tables and indexes, and browsing, editing, adding, deleting and searching records. It can import and export records as text, tables from and to CSV files, and databases from and to SQL dump files. Users can issue SQL queries and inspect results, review a log of executed SQL commands, and plot simple graphs from table or query data. The README states it is not meant to replace a spreadsheet application.
use_cases: browse and edit SQLite database contents
import or export CSV files to SQLite
export a database to an SQL dump file
run and inspect SQL queries on a SQLite file
plot simple graphs from query results
how_to_run: Other platforms: compile using the instructions in BUILDING.md
notable: Spreadsheet-style interface aimed at users who do not know SQL
Log of all SQL commands the application issues
Available through many package managers across Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, and Nix
Continuous and nightly builds for AppImage, macOS, and Windows
Wiki with user and developer documentation
caveats: The README says it is not meant to replace a spreadsheet application and omits some spreadsheet-style features on purpose
Distribution packages may be older versions, per the Debian section
Other Linux distributions require compiling from source using BUILDING.md
